rules.title: Just cause required to evict tenants in units covered by the Rent Ordinance
rules.requirement: A landlord can only evict you from a unit covered by the SF Rent Ordinance for one of 17 listed just causes, and that cause must be the landlord's dominant motive. A lease simply expiring or the building being sold is not a just cause, and a landlord also needs just cause to remove housing services such as parking, storage, or laundry.

coverage.summary: Rental units covered by the San Francisco Rent Ordinance. This includes units exempt from the rent increase limits, such as units first certified for occupancy after June 13, 1979, tenancies eligible for Costa-Hawkins rent increases, and some tenancies whose rent is regulated by another government agency.

rules.penalty: A landlord who evicts or tries to evict a tenant unlawfully may face substantial civil and/or criminal liability.
rules.quoted_span: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction. Note that the mere expiration of a rental agreement or a change in ownership does not constitute "just cause" for eviction.
rules.interaction: Just cause protections also cover tenancies that are exempt from local rent limits under the state Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act.

rules.title: Rent Ordinance rent increase limits: exemption for units certified after June 13, 1979
rules.requirement: Units that first obtained a Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979 are exempt from the SF Rent Ordinance's rent increase limits, although they keep just cause eviction protection. If your unit was certified for occupancy on or before that date, it may be subject to the Ordinance's rent increase limits.

coverage.summary: The Rent Ordinance rent increase limits do not apply to units that first obtained a Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979. They also do not apply to tenancies eligible for rent increases under Costa-Hawkins or to some units whose rent is regulated by another government agency.

rules.exemptions: Units first certified for occupancy after June 13, 1979; Costa-Hawkins-eligible tenancies; some units whose rent is regulated by another government agency.
rules.quoted_span: This includes tenancies in newly constructed rental units that first obtained a Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979
rules.interaction: Tenancies eligible for rent increases under the state Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act are exempt from the local rent increase limits.

notes: The page is mainly about just cause eviction. A rent_increase_limits record was added only to carry the June 13, 1979 Certificate of Occupancy cutoff that the page states. The page gives no rent cap formula, so key_value is null, and the citation section for that record is inferred.
